findings.body: `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` implements `deleteManyByCredential()` (line 23) even though `ICalendarCacheRepository` (the interface it declares to implement) has no such method — the real repository deletes cache via `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany` directly in `GoogleCalendarService.unwatchCalendar` and the new `deleteCacheHandler`, not through the repository interface. This is dead surface area on the mock that suggests a contract that doesn't exist; if the interface later changes, the mock will silently drift. Either add `deleteManyByCredential` to `ICalendarCacheRepository` (and implement it on the real repository, then use it in `deleteCache.handler.ts` and `unwatchCalendar`) so cache deletion goes through the repository abstraction consistently, or remove the stray mock method.

findings.title: credentialIds may contain null/undefined for delegation credentials, producing a useless IN query and wrong cache mapping
findings.body: The handler builds `credentialIds` with `connectedCalendars.map((cal) => cal.credentialId)` and passes them to `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`, which does `where: { credentialId: { in: credentialIds } }`. For delegation-credential calendars, `credentialId` can be null/absent (the codebase uses `isInMemoryDelegationCredential` / negative ids and `delegationCredentialId` instead — see `getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts` and the repository's own comments about in-memory delegation credentials having no valid credentialId). Passing nulls into a Prisma `in` filter either throws or silently matches nothing, and the resulting `cacheStatusMap` is keyed by real credential ids, so delegated calendars will always get `cacheUpdatedAt: null` even when a userId-keyed cache exists. The handler should filter out non-positive/null credential ids before the query (mirroring `assertCalendarHasDbCredential`'s `credentialId < 0` guard) and handle the delegation-credential case explicitly.

findings.title: macOS-only sed syntax breaks the script on Linux, and it mutates a shared .env file
findings.body: The script uses `sed -i '' -E ...` (line 68), which is the BSD/macOS form of in-place sed; on GNU/Linux `sed -i ''` treats `''` as a file name and fails, so the `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` is never updated on Linux dev machines. Additionally, the script writes directly into `../.env` (a shared, git-ignored but developer-critical file), creating it if missing and overwriting an existing `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` — a destructive side effect for a helper script that should be opt-in. Use a portable in-place approach (e.g. a temp file + `mv`, or `sed -i.bak` with cleanup) and avoid silently creating/overwriting `.env`; at minimum guard the write behind a confirmation or write to a clearly-named override file.

findings.title: Migration warning comment contradicts the actual migration (column is added WITH a default)
findings.body: The migration's header warning states: "Added the required column `updatedAt` to the `CalendarCache` table without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty." But the very next statement is `ALTER TABLE "CalendarCache" ADD COLUMN "updatedAt" TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW();`, which adds the column WITH a default, so the warning is factually wrong and the migration is safe on non-empty tables. The stale Prisma-generated warning (left over from before the author added `DEFAULT NOW()`) should be removed or corrected, otherwise reviewers and future readers will believe the migration is unsafe and may attempt to rewrite it.

findings.title: Cache status row is rendered as an interactive DropdownMenuItem with no action, trapping clicks and confusing users
findings.body: The cache status display (lines 84-97) is wrapped in a `<DropdownMenuItem className="focus:ring-muted">` even though it performs no action — it is purely informational. In Radix dropdowns, a `DropdownMenuItem` is an interactive, focusable, clickable element; rendering a non-interactive status inside one means clicking the status row closes the menu (standard item behavior) and it can steal keyboard focus from the real actions, which is an accessibility and UX defect. The status should be rendered as a non-interactive element (e.g. a plain `<div>` with appropriate padding, or `DropdownMenuLabel`/`DropdownMenuSeparator` semantics) inside `DropdownMenuContent`, not as a `DropdownMenuItem`.

findings.title: ConnectedCalendarList receives disableConnectionModification but the wrapper computes shouldDisableConnectionModification and never passes it down
findings.body: The wrapper computes `shouldDisableConnectionModification = isDisabled || disableConnectionModification` (line 166) and passes it only to `SelectedCalendarsSettingsHeading` (to hide the "Add" selector). However, `ConnectedCalendarList` is rendered with `disableConnectionModification={disableConnectionModification}` (line 182) — the raw prop — not `shouldDisableConnectionModification`. `isDisabled` is true when `disabledScope === scope`, i.e. when the current scope is locked; in that state the heading correctly hides connection modification, but each `CredentialActionsDropdown` still receives `disableConnectionModification=false` and will render the "Remove App" action, letting users disconnect an integration while the scope is supposed to be read-only. The list should receive `shouldDisableConnectionModification` so the per-credential actions respect the disabled scope.

findings.title: Unused CalendarsRouterHandlerCache type left in the router file
findings.body: The file declares `type CalendarsRouterHandlerCache = { connectedCalendars?: ...; setDestinationCalendar?: ... }` (lines 8-11) but nothing references it — the handlers are imported dynamically inline in each procedure. It's dead code that will drift out of sync as handlers are added (it already omits `deleteCache`). Remove it or actually use it; as-is it's misleading.

findings.title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds return type uses updatedAt: Date | null but the implementation can return null for credentials with no rows only via absence, not per-row null
findings.body: The interface declares `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds(credentialIds: number[]): Promise<{ credentialId: number; updatedAt: Date | null }[]>`. The implementation maps `prisma.calendarCache.groupBy` results, where `_max.updatedAt` is `Date | null` (null only if all grouped rows have null updatedAt — which cannot happen now that the column is `NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()`). More importantly, credentials with no cache rows are simply absent from the result array, so callers must distinguish "absent" from "present with null". The `| null` in the type is misleading given the NOT NULL column, and the contract would be clearer if the method either returned a status for every requested id (with null for missing) or the type documented that only credentials with rows are returned. The current handler works around this with `cacheStatusMap.get(...) || null`, but the interface should make the absence semantics explicit.
